narrative.overview: The site presents every credibility claim as an official stamped service record rather than a marketing promise. Trust is proven the way a real shop proves it: dated ledger entries, inked seals, ring-stamped badges, a typewriter ticket face for dates and labels. The world deliberately refuses both auto-shop defaults: no checkered-flag/racing-stripe motifs, and no sterile tech-startup gloss. Color is almost entirely achromatic (warm paper, ink, steel); the two stamp-ink colors carry nearly all of the site's chroma, sourced from the shop's own logo mark rather than a generic palette choice. The brand teal (#0e4b5e) is sampled directly from the shop's logo (public/logo.jpg, measured average ~#0e4b5e, per PRODUCT.md's Brand Commitments), not an invented accent. Its reach is deliberately wider than a pure mark-only ink: beyond stamp/seal/badge rings, it also colors the header's AUTOMOTIVE subline, the secondary Call button, the circle/scallop service-badge icon fills, and link hovers on dark surfaces (footer, visit card), so the shop's own brand color reads as a recognizable identity thread, not a rare accent, while still never becoming a background fill or large field. The one confirmed exception is .btn-kuruma, the KurumaWorks booking button, which uses KurumaWorks blue (#2663eb), a standing cross-site brand requirement from the reusable KurumaWorks template (PRODUCT.md > Brand Commitments), not a local palette choice. It is intentionally excluded from the brand-teal system so the booking action reads identically across every business site on the template.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper/ink/steel palette, with stamp teal (sampled from the shop's own logo) and stamp red as the system's only chroma
Big Shoulders for display numerals and headlines only; Libre Franklin for all body/UI; Courier Prime confined to micro-labels and dates
Hairline-rule section dividers, never shadow-card chrome
A shared SVG ink-edge filter (feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap) textures every stamp, seal, and badge ring identically
Ledger entries accumulate into view with an exponential ease-out, never a bounce

rules.name: The Logo-Teal Rule
rules.body: Stamp teal is the shop's own measured logo color, not an invented accent. It appears in stamp/seal/badge marks and in a defined, closed set of brand-carrying UI details (header subline, secondary button, service icon fills, dark-surface link hovers via its light variant). It never fills a background, a large field, or an element outside that set.

rules.name: The KurumaWorks Exception
rules.body: `.btn-kuruma` is the standing exception to the Logo-Teal Rule: it always uses KurumaWorks blue, sourced from the cross-site booking template, regardless of the host site's own palette.

rules.name: The Three-Tier Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders is for display/numerals only, Libre Franklin is for all body and UI text, and Courier Prime is for micro-labels and dates only. No face crosses into another's role anywhere on the page.

rules.name: The No-Card-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No shadow-card chrome appears on any content panel, ledger entry, or service panel. Shadows are reserved for elements that are literally fixed/sticky above the page (header once scrolled, mobile bar).

dos: Do confine Big Shoulders to display/numeral roles, Libre Franklin to body/UI, and Courier Prime to micro-labels/dates; never mix roles.
Do keep stamp teal and stamp red inside stamp/seal/badge marks, plus the closed set of brand-carrying details named in the Logo-Teal Rule.
Do use the shared #ink-edge filter for any new stamp, seal, or badge element so the ink-textured edge stays consistent.
Do use hairline rules (--paper-line / --dark-paper-line) to separate sections.

Do use cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) exponential ease-out for reveal/settle motion; pair any IntersectionObserver reveal with a scroll-based fallback so content isn't permanently hidden on fast/instant scroll.
donts: Don't wash stamp teal or stamp red across a background, large field, or component outside the defined mark and brand-detail set.
Don't recolor .btn-kuruma to match this site's local palette; it is a fixed cross-site brand exception.
Don't add shadow-card chrome to panels, ledger entries, or service badges; shadows are reserved for genuinely fixed/sticky elements.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing anywhere; motion settles, it doesn't overshoot.
Don't introduce kickers/eyebrows, hard-offset neobrutalist shadows, glyph icon fonts, or system display faces; none exist in the shipped build, and none fit this restrained, ink-stamped world.
